clues: This port town is on the coast of Pakistan, by the Arabian Sea. Oman lies just across the sea from it.
Cool sea currents keep this desert port less hot in summer than towns far inland. Its winter nights also stay warm, thanks to the same sea.
This town began late in the 1600s as a small fishing village. It grew into a trade hub under the rule of Oman.
In 1954, experts from the United States picked this spot for a deep-water port. At the time, Oman still ruled the town from across the sea.
For a long time, this town was a far-off piece of Oman, across the sea. Pakistan bought it in 1958, and it has been Pakistani ever since.
